messages.author: a68df3015a3e3c69
messages.subject: install without root?
parts: I was wondering if its possible to install revolution r open in the home directory of a linux server where I don't have root access?

messages.author: 9ca0345d553844f2
messages.subject: Re: install without root?
parts:
Hi Jake,

Here’s the way an rpm install can be done by a non-root user:


Unpack the installation tarball to find the rpm.

 

mkdir $HOME/localrpmdb

rpm --initdb --dbpath $HOME/localrpmdb

export MY_RPM_DBPATH=$HOME/localrpmdb && \

    rpm --dbpath $MY_RPM_DBPATH --prefix $HOME \

    --nodeps -i RRO-*.x86_64.rpm

 

For a Debian package manager, use this:

 dpkg -i --force-not-root --root=$HOME package.deb


Let me know how that goes for you.


Thanks,

Josée Martens

messages.author: 2aed7cbfca222ffd
messages.subject: Re: install without root?
parts:
Hello Jake,

We have confirmed that their is a general problem with non-root installs and we will be working on a fix for this issue.

For the time being, you will need to either install the software as the root user or a user with 'sudo' privileges, that is listed
in the sudoers file.

Here is more information on setting up the 'sudoers' file:
https://www.linux.com/component/content/article/133-general-linux/397711


We hope to have this problem fixed in our next release, which will be in late January of 2016.

Stephen Weller
Revolution R Open Support Engineer

messages.author: 829e33684ea2ecd2
messages.subject: Re: install without root?
parts:
Hi Jake,

If I understand correctly, you are trying to install the MKL after installing Micorosoft R Open to a non-default folder.
Unfortunately, I don't think we support that kind of configuration directly at the moment, though we certainly should.

You can work around the issue however by manually installing the MKL files to the proper location as follows:

1).  Cd to the directory '$RHOME/lib64/R/lib on your system( by default this is '/usr/lib64/MRO-3.2.3/R-3.2.3/lib64/R/lib')
2).  Rename the files 'libRlapack.so' and 'libRblas.so' to 'libRlapack.so.keep' and 'libRblas.so.keep'.
3).  Change directory to the directory where you installed the 'RevoMath' folder.
4).  Copy all of the files in this folder to the '$RHOME/lib64/R/lib' folder.
5).  Install the 'RevoUtilsMath' package as follows:   'R CMD INSTALL RevoUtilsMath.tar.gz'


This manual install should work - let me know if you have any problems with it.


Stephen Weller
Microsoft R Open Technical Support

Unfortunately, I don't think we support that kind of configuration directly at the moment, though we certainly should.

You can work around the issue however by manually installing the MKL files to the proper location as follows:

1).  Cd to the directory '$RHOME/lib64/R/lib on your system( by default this is '/usr/lib64/MRO-3.2.3/R-3.2.3/lib64/R/lib')
2).  Rename the files 'libRlapack.so' and 'libRblas.so' to 'libRlapack.so.keep' and 'libRblas.so.keep'.
3).  Change directory to the directory where you installed the 'RevoMath' folder.
4).  Copy all of the files in this folder to the '$RHOME/lib64/R/lib' folder.
5).  Install the 'RevoUtilsMath' package as follows:   'R CMD INSTALL RevoUtilsMath.tar.gz'


This manual install should work - let me know if you have any problems with it.


Stephen Weller
Microsoft R Open Technical Support
